 10 Ways Through U.S. Airports And Borders Including The $45 TSA ConfirmID

 Justin Fenwick is a travel journalist who specializes in national parks and outdoor travel reporting. He covers the stories that shape how people plan and experience their trips across the United States.

 Navigating U.S. airports and borders in November 2026 requires more than just a valid ticket and a carry-on bag. Since the full enforcement of REAL ID standards began in May 2025, the landscape of acceptable identification has shifted significantly for domestic travelers.

 Those who arrived at the airport without a compliant license or a passport book found themselves facing stricter verification protocols than in years past. Fortunately, the Department of Homeland Security and various international agencies have expanded the toolkit of credentials available to the modern traveler, ranging from five-year trusted traveler memberships to temporary digital solutions.
 This list highlights the ten most effective ways to move through security checkpoints and international arrival halls as of late 2026.

 From REAL ID to Touchless ID, TSA screening has changed. These 7 rules explain what travelers can expect at U.S. airport checkpoints.
 Posts 
 By  
 Felix Ngeso 
 TSA PreCheck
 TSA precheck fast lane line before security at Reagan National Airport Credit: David Tran Photo/Shutterstock 
 TSA PreCheck remains the primary choice for travelers who mostly fly within the United States. This program allows members to use dedicated security lanes where they do not have to remove shoes, belts, light jackets, laptops, or 3-1-1 liquids. As of late 2026, enrollment fees vary slightly depending on the service provider, ranging from $79.75 through IDEMIA to $85 through Telos , with memberships lasting for five years.
 Recent updates have made the program even more accessible for younger passengers. According to the TSA , travelers aged 30 and under can save $20 on their membership as part of a new initiative launched in April 2026. This move has encouraged a broader demographic to join the millions of existing members who enjoy shorter wait times.
 Global Entry
 Global Entry Kiosk Credit: Shvetsa/Pexels 
 Global Entry is designed for travelers who frequently return to the United States from abroad. Administered by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), it allows pre-approved, low-risk travelers to bypass traditional passport control lines. Members use automated kiosks or mobile apps at select airports to complete their entry process. Earlier this year, the application fee for this five-year membership was adjusted to $120. 
 One of the most significant advantages of this program is that it includes TSA PreCheck benefits at no additional cost. According to CBP officials , the program requires a rigorous background check and an in-person interview before approval is granted. While wait times for these interviews can be variable, the long-term time savings upon arrival in the U.S. are substantial.
 For those who travel outside the country even once or twice a year, the $120 investment is often viewed as a superior value to standalone PreCheck. It effectively streamlines the entire airport experience from departure to return.
 NEXUS
 Nexus Card with a Canadian Passport Credit: Sadi Hockmuller/Shutterstock 
 NEXUS is often described by frequent flyers as the best-kept secret in the Trusted Traveler Program portfolio. It is a joint program between the U.S. and Canada that facilitates expedited processing for air, land, and sea travelers between the two nations. Earlier in 2026, the fee for NEXUS was increased to $120 to align with other programs, but it remains a powerhouse of benefits.
 A single NEXUS membership provides the benefits of both TSA PreCheck and Global Entry, making it a comprehensive solution for North American residents. According to the Canada Border Services Agency , the program is open to citizens and permanent residents of both countries. It is particularly useful for those who live near the border and use land crossings frequently.
 This program earns its place here due to its sheer versatility. Many travelers comparing TSA PreCheck, CLEAR, and Touchless ID are discovering that NEXUS offers broader coverage than Global Entry at the same price. It is the ultimate choice for those who want maximum border flexibility.
 TSA ConfirmID
 Departing passengers wait at TSA checkpoints inside Louis Armstrong airport Credit: Elliott Cowand Jr/Shutterstock 
 TSA ConfirmID is the newest addition to the airport security landscape, having launched on February 1, 2026. This service was created to assist travelers who arrive at the airport without a REAL ID or another form of acceptable identification. For a $45 fee , the TSA performs an enhanced identity verification process that allows the traveler to proceed to the screening area.
 Unlike the five-year memberships mentioned above, ConfirmID is a trip-specific solution. As noted by Department of Defense travel updates , the verification is valid for a 10-day period to cover both the departure and the return flight. It relies on third-party data and identity questions to confirm the passenger is who they claim to be.
 This service is on the list because it acts as a critical backup for travelers in a bind. Even though the TSA issues a final warning over the $45 fee for those who fail to bring proper ID, the existence of ConfirmID prevents people from being completely stranded. It is a pragmatic, if expensive, tool for emergency situations.
 Mobile Passport Control
 Mobile Passport Control app airport Credit: Shutterstock 
 Mobile Passport Control (MPC) is a free alternative to Global Entry that does not require a background check or a five-year commitment. It is a mobile application that allows U.S. citizens and Canadian visitors to submit their passport and customs declaration information digitally before arriving at the airport. This often grants them access to a dedicated lane that moves faster than the standard line.
 The app has seen significant expansion throughout 2026, now covering more land borders and even general aviation ports. According to official CBP documentation , travelers can create a profile and submit their information as soon as they land. This eliminates the need for paper forms and reduces the time spent interacting with a CBP officer.
 For families or infrequent international travelers who do not want to pay for Global Entry, MPC is a highly effective way to save time. It proves that expedited travel does not always have to come with a premium price tag.
 REAL ID Compliant Licenses
 TSA officer handling REAL ID to a traveler Credit: Shutterstock 
 As of November 2026, a REAL ID compliant driver's license or state ID is the mandatory minimum for any adult traveler who does not wish to carry a passport for domestic flights. These licenses are marked with a star in the upper right corner, signifying that the issuing state has met federal security standards. Enforcement of this rule has been in full effect since May 2025.
 Travelers who have not yet upgraded their licenses may find themselves redirected to the ConfirmID process or denied boarding entirely. As reported by Yahoo Travel , the transition to REAL ID has been a multi-year effort that finally culminated in strict checkpoint enforcement. Each state sets its own fee for these IDs, typically ranging from $30 to $60.
 While it does not grant access to expedited lanes, it is the barrier to entry for the airport itself. Maintaining a compliant license is the simplest way to avoid the fees and delays associated with secondary identity verification.
 U.S. Passport Book
 Person holding American passport Credit: KieferPix/Shutterstock 
 The U.S. passport book remains the most powerful identity document a traveler can own. It is valid for all international travel by air, land, or sea, and it serves as a federally recognized REAL ID for domestic flights. In 2026, the total cost for a first-time adult passport book is $165, which includes the application fee and the execution fee.
 Passports are valid for ten years for adults, making the annual cost relatively low compared to other memberships. The State Department has continued to modernize the application process, offering online renewals for $130 for many eligible citizens . This has helped keep processing times manageable even during peak travel seasons.
 U.S. Passport Card
 Specimen of the U.S. passport card, issued by the State Department Credit: U.S. Department of State,  Wikimedia Commons 
 For travelers who primarily visit Canada, Mexico, or the Caribbean by car or cruise ship, the U.S. passport card is a cost-effective alternative to the book. It is a wallet-sized card that is valid for land and sea border crossings within the Western Hemisphere. First-time adult applicants currently pay $65 total for this document. 
 While the card is not valid for international air travel, it is fully compliant with REAL ID standards for domestic flights. Many travelers find that a passport card is cheaper than the passport book while still providing a federally issued identity document. It also allows for the use of Ready Lanes at land border crossings, which can speed up the process for motorists.
 This document belongs on the list because it fills a specific niche for budget-conscious travelers. It provides the security and identification benefits of a passport without the higher price tag of the full book. It is an ideal secondary document for those who want a backup ID that fits easily in a wallet.
 Enhanced Driver's License (EDL)
 Enhanced driver's licenses Credit:  United States Department of Homeland Security /Wikimedia Commons 
 Residents of Michigan, Minnesota, New York, Vermont, and Washington have access to an Enhanced Driver's License (EDL). This document serves as both a REAL ID compliant license and a Western Hemisphere Travel Initiative (WHTI) compliant document. It allows the holder to cross the border into Canada or Mexico by land or sea without a passport.
 The EDL contains a vicinity chip that speeds up the border crossing process by allowing CBP officers to pull up the traveler's information as they approach the booth. According to TSA guidelines , these licenses are fully accepted at airport checkpoints. They typically cost about $30 more than a standard license, depending on the state.
 The EDL is included here because it represents the most efficient single document for land-border residents. It eliminates the need to carry both a license and a passport card, combining their functions into one piece of plastic. For those in the five participating states, it is often the most practical identification choice available.
 SENTRI
 Membership card of SENTRI program Credit:  Department of Homeland Security / Wikimedia Commons 
 The Secure Electronic Network for Travelers Rapid Inspection (SENTRI) is a program specifically designed for travelers frequently crossing the U.S. and Mexico border . It provides expedited processing through dedicated lanes at land ports of entry. Like Global Entry and NEXUS, the fee for SENTRI has been unified at $120 for a five-year membership in late 2026. 
 While SENTRI is primarily used for land crossings, members who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents also receive TSA PreCheck benefits. This makes it a useful tool for southern border residents who also fly domestically. The application process involves a background check and a thorough vehicle inspection if the member plans to drive across the border.
 This program closes the list because it addresses the specific needs of travelers in the southern United States. It provides a high level of security and efficiency for those who navigate the unique challenges of the Mexican border. By offering a combination of land and air benefits, it ensures that frequent crossers have a reliable way to manage their transit throughout the year.
